summary: Ephemeral socket coalescing breakdown causing periodic 5xx cycles and GPU context swap failures
description:
Issue summary:
Customers on a subset of Dedicated pools (Acme Commerce) reported recurring waves of 502/503 errors during a high-concurrency burst window. The errors coincided with streaming sessions being torn down and many short-lived TLS handshakes. Support observed an elevated p50->p99 error rate and correlated spikes in runtime GPU context swap failures (NVML resets reported in the runtime logs).

Impact:
- Multiple Acme customer endpoints experienced degraded availability for ~27 minutes across a ~45 minute incident window.
- Higher error rate for streaming sessions and short-text generation (p50 latency increased 2x, p99 failed requests rose to ~8%).
- Internal dashboards showed accept queue depth oscillations and ephemeral socket reuse failures on a subset of apigw nodes.

Timeline (local times):
- 2026-03-10 18:03 UTC: First alert from monitoring (apigw group) - error-rate jump to 6% 5xx for tenant pool A.
- 2026-03-10 18:06 UTC: Support triage, customer informed.
- 2026-03-10 18:09 UTC: SRE identified increased TLS session cache evictions on apigw and repeated short-lived TCP connections from tenant.
- 2026-03-10 18:15 UTC: Runtime team observed GPU context swap timeouts co-occurring with request fanout and prefetch locks.
- 2026-03-10 18:30 UTC: Mitigation (temporary) applied: increased keepalive and accept-queue headroom on affected apigw pool.
- 2026-03-10 18:55 UTC: 5xx rate back to baseline; incident declared resolved.

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) On a dedicated tenant driving high numbers of short streaming sessions with frequent TLS renegotiation, ramp to 800-1,200 concurrent short-lived streams.
2) Observe accept queue growth on a small fraction of apigw nodes and TLS session cache churn.
3) If priority route migration starts concurrently (weight rebalance triggered by autoscaler), the combination can starve ephemeral socket coalescing and trigger retries, surfacing 5xx at the gateway and causing the runtime to attempt aggressive GPU context swap/eviction.

Logs / observations:
- apigw stderr: repeated "session_cache_evict: shard=11 entries=1200" logs around 18:08-18:12 UTC.
- apigw metrics: accept_queue_depth_peek spike to 320 on 3/12 nodes, backlog increased CPU sys % on those nodes.
- runtime logs: "gpu_context_swap_timeout: uid=acme-tenant-12 task=fanout prefetch_lock=held" followed by NVML warning messages and elevated OOM-retry entries.
- No evidence of hardware faults; pins showed typical GPU memory accounting.

Initial hypothesis:
- TLS session cache fragmentation and aggressive session eviction prevented socket coalescing for keepalives, creating many short-lived TCP handoffs.
- Concurrent priority route migration caused a subset of requests to be re-routed mid-flow, amplifying connection churn.
- The runtime's current GPU context swap path is sensitive to repeated prefetch cancellations and can escalate to transient context swap timeouts under this specific I/O pattern.

Suggested mitigation applied during incident:
- Bumped apigw keepalive timeout and increased accept-queue size for the affected nodes to allow sockets to reuse instead of re-handshaking.
- Disabled route weight migration for the affected tenant pool for the next 6 hours to avoid flapping during warmup.
- Throttled tenant burst to dedicated pool to reduce immediate fanout and prefetch pressure.
investigation_notes: Confirmed accept queue spikes map 1:1 with TLS eviction logs on apigw nodes (logs: apigw-az1-13, apigw-az1-14).
Heap of short-lived sockets prevented HTTP/2 STREAM coalescing; many connections were falling back to new TLS handshakes.
Runtime team reproduced increased gpu_context_swap latency in staging by replaying similar short-stream traffic with concurrent route weight changes.
Hypothesis validated: combination of TLS cache fragmentation + priority migration produced non-linear amplification of connection churn.
NVML warnings were transient and no permanent GPU loss observed; runtime patch will add backoff/resume semantics for context swaps.
Linked runbooks consulted: apigw-connection-thrashing and runtime-gpu-prefetch.
Customer impact was limited to a dedicated tenant pool; no cross-tenant data exposure noted.
Note: this incident surface differed from standard-prefetch OOM cases — the signal was primarily at the gateway accept layer.
Investigating long-term fix: improve TLS session shard eviction algorithm and add a runtime safeguard to delay GPU context swap during high prefetch cancellation rates.
comments: Support (2026-03-10 18:07 UTC) - Priya: Reached out to Acme Commerce. Confirmed they saw elevated 5xx and temporary streaming disconnects; asked for any recent client changes.
Customer (2026-03-10 18:09 UTC) - Acme SRE: No client code change; traffic pattern increased due to a campaign. We're seeing many short sessions (20-200ms).
SRE (2026-03-10 18:18 UTC) - Jonah Burns: Observed TLS shard evictions on three apigw nodes. Bumped keepalive, increasing immediate stability.
Runtime (2026-03-10 18:40 UTC) - Mei Chen: Reproduced context-swap timeouts in staging with a traffic replay. Preparing PR to add conservative backoff on swap scheduling.
Support (2026-03-10 19:05 UTC) - Priya: Customer confirmed traffic returned to normal; provided thanks. Agreed to follow up once permanent fixes are deployed.
Post-incident (2026-03-11 09:30 UTC) - Ethan Kim: Backported apigw session-cache fix and deployed runtime PR in canary; monitoring for regressions.
resolution: Short-term: temporarily increased apigw keepalive and accept-queue headroom for affected apigw pool; disabled priority route migrations for the tenant pool while the customer ran their campaign.
Medium-term: backported apigw patch to reduce shard eviction aggressiveness and improved acceptance logging (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/apigw/pull/732).

Long-term: runtime change to add swap backoff when prefetch_cancel rate > threshold and an alert to correlate accept-queue spikes with TLS eviction metrics (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1284).
Runbook updates: added 'tls-cache-fragmentation' section to apigw connection thrashing runbook and a checklist for temporarily disabling route migration during large tenant bursts.
Customer follow-up: arranged a post-incident review with Acme on 2026-03-15 to review traffic shaping and dedicated pool settings.
Status: Resolved - mitigations applied and code/fixes merged to main; monitoring shows no recurrence for two full 24h periods since fix rollout.
